pitch.title: Thomas Edison and the Ten Thousand Failures
pitch.hook: Ten thousand failed lightbulbs piled up in a New Jersey laboratory.
pitch.angle: People think failure means stopping, but Edison treated every wrong material as a finished answer.
key_facts: Thomas Edison tested thousands of materials for the lightbulb filament
A reporter asked Edison how it felt to fail ten thousand times
Edison stated he had not failed, but found ten thousand ways that did not work
The incandescent bulb eventually glowed bright using a carbonized bamboo filament

script.title: Thomas Edison and the Ten Thousand Failures

beats.narration: Ten thousand burnt filaments piled up in a dark New Jersey laboratory in eighteen seventy nine.
beats.image_prompt: Moody cinematic photo of a pile of charred delicate wires on a dark wooden workshop table, dim warm lighting, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: Most inventors saw a broken wire as a ruined experiment that wasted valuable time.
beats.image_prompt: Moody cinematic photo of a cracked glass bulb with a melted filament on a cluttered 19th century workbench, soft amber glow, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: So a curious reporter asked Thomas Edison how it felt to fail ten thousand times in a row.
beats.image_prompt: Cinematic shot from behind a person holding a vintage notebook in a dimly lit Victorian laboratory, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: Edison insisted he made zero mistakes.
beats.image_prompt: Cinematic close up photo of a hand writing chemical notes in a leather journal with an ink pen, moody lighting, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: He had simply identified ten thousand materials that would never work.
beats.image_prompt: Moody cinematic photo of glass jars filled with various plant fibers and threads on dark wooden shelves, warm accent light, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: Then he tried a strip of carbonized bamboo, and the bulb stayed lit for over twelve hundred hours.
beats.image_prompt: Cinematic shot of a single glass filament incandescent bulb shining bright golden light in a pitch black room, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

beats.narration: Elimination is just discovery in disguise.
beats.image_prompt: Dramatic moody photograph of a glowing glass lightbulb casting a strong golden beam across an empty dark workshop, film grain, vertical 9:16 framing, subject centered, no text, no faces

fact_check.claim: Thomas Edison tested thousands of materials for the lightbulb filament.
A reporter asked Edison about failing ten thousand times.
Edison stated he had found thousands of ways that did not work.
A carbonized bamboo filament was successfully used to keep the bulb glowing.
